entities.summary:
Ludger was a 8th-century missionary who played a pivotal role in the conversion of the Frisians and Saxons to Christianity. Born of unknown parentage, Ludger is believed to have been born in the early 8th century, although the exact date is not certain.

As a missionary, Ludger was instrumental in the establishment of Werden Abbey, a major center of Christian learning and missionary activity. He was also appointed as the first Bishop of Münster in Westphalia, a region that would become a major hub of power and influence in the Holy Roman Empire.

Ludger's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped to lay the foundations for the spread of Christianity throughout Northern Europe. His influence can still be seen in the many monasteries and churches that he founded, and his reputation as a missionary and church leader has endured for centuries.

As the 'Apostle of Saxony', Ludger's name has become synonymous with the conversion of the Saxons to Christianity. His work continues to be celebrated and studied by historians and scholars today, who are fascinated by the complex and often fraught process of missionary work in medieval Europe.
